messages:
Maria: heads-up — I'm kicking off a per-tier canary for model-X v2 limited to Enterprise + eu-west for 10% traffic. I noticed the smart router's fallback mapping could divert to v1-quant (us-central) when capacity is low. want to align on expectations for: exposure accounting, quota impact, and console UX for scoping. https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/rl-983

Ajay: quick question — is the canary implemented as a routing policy slice (i.e. runtime routing) or as a config-only rollout (control-plane flag)?

Maria: runtime slice. policy looks like this in the rollout object:
```json
{
  "scope": { "tiers": ["enterprise"], "regions": ["eu-west"] },
  "variants": [{"id":"v2","weight":10},{"id":"v1-quant","weight":90}],
  "fallbacks": ["v1-quant"]
}
```

Carmen: thanks. two things: (1) when fallback routes to a variant in a different region we currently don't adjust quota meters per-tier-per-region, so billing/usage could be misattributed. (2) telemetry dashboard currently attributes success/latency to the receiving variant only, which hides exposure for the intended canary.

Leo: +1 on telemetry. We should create a synthetic dimension: requested_variant vs executed_variant so we can tell when the smart router swapped. That will help SLOs.

Ajay: on quotas — if enterprise eu-west requests are routed to us-central v1-quant, do we decrement enterprise eu-west reserved capacity or us-central pool? We need to decide default behavior (charge by request origin vs execution location).

Maria: prefer origin-based accounting for quota consumption (so enterprise sees usage against their commitment). But cost attribution for infra billing should include execution location. We need both views in Console.

Carmen: UX ask: in the rollout UI, we should show a small badge when cross-region fallback is possible: "may execute in other region" with a link to explain cost/latency implications. Otherwise PMs assume all traffic stays in EU.

Leo: Edge case — sticky sessions and KV cache affinity. If a client gets routed to v2 on first request then subsequent tokens hit cache paths; but if later fallback sends to v1 we may miss cache and latency spikes. We should add a heuristic to prefer variants that share the same cache keyspace for sticky traffic.

Ajay: implementation options: (A) extend routing policy with "affinity_group" and prefer variants with same affinity, (B) inject a cache-affinity header at routing time so execution nodes can map. both need telemetry and dashboard surfaces.

Maria: agree. short term: add request/exec variant dims to telemetry and log a "routing_reason" tag (capacity, quota-exceed, health, rollout-exposure). Long term: add affinity-aware fallback ranking.

Carmen: operational note — add an alert: when executed_variant != requested_variant for >2% of canary traffic for 5min, page eng-platform. That would catch accidental wide fallback.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout rl-983 started by Maria at 1971800001 (scope: Enterprise / eu-west / 10%).

Leo: small API naming nit: current rollout API uses `scope` and `variants` but no explicit `fallback_policy`. Let's propose `fallback_policy: { mode: "regional-preference" | "strict-origin" | "affinity-aware" }` so operators can pick behavior.

Ajay: +1. default should be `regional-preference` (optimize latency/cost) but enterprise customers can set `strict-origin` to ensure data locality and quota alignment.

Maria: I'll file a short RFC and a Console mockup. Action items: Carmen to add telemetry dims + alert, Ajay to propose API extension, Leo to sketch affinity heuristic, Maria to draft RFC and update rollout page copy.

Carmen: ETA on telemetry changes ~2 days. I'll add a temporary grafana dashboard panel for requested_vs_executed counts.

Ajay: I'll draft API PR today, include migration notes for existing rollouts.

Maria: thanks all — let's keep this thread for updates. :rocket:
